alex.k: Heads-up: saw a production spike this morning — requests routed to AMD nodes fell back to the generic fp16 kernel for certain sequence buckets, latency +120ms on p50 for batch=1, seq=1024. Investigating.
sagar: Ack. Which op / kernel is missing? can you paste the kernel registry check? :eyes:
alex.k: pasted quick outputs from the runtime kernel registry:
```text
rocm-kernel-registry --model gpt-13b --arch gfx1030 --seq 1024
available_kernels: [matmul_fp16_generic, softmax_fp32]
optimized_kernels: [matmul_fp16_512_only]
missing: [matmul_fp16_1024, kv-cache-stepped]
```
Also saw this in the runtime log right before the fallback:
```log
2026-11-03T09:12:43Z runtime: kernel lookup failed for matmul(fp16,seq=1024): NOT_FOUND
2026-11-03T09:12:43Z routing: selecting fallback path 'generic-fp16' for node=ami-rocm-4
2026-11-03T09:12:43Z perf: token_latency=245ms
```
mei: hmm. That matches the autotuner outputs we shipped last week — it only generated specialized matmul kernels for seq <= 512 on gfx1030. We didn't binary-blast for 1024 because of compile time constraints. We should've published an explicit availability-map so the router doesn't assume a kernel exists.

tasha: we can add a conditional routing rule as a stopgap. Suggest config like:
```yaml
routing:
  policies:
    - name: rocm_seq_guard
      when:
        - target: device.family == "gfx10" and request.seq_len >= 768
      action: route_to: fallback_pool (nvidia or cpu)
      reason: avoid rocm missing-specialized-kernel fallback
```
This would keep AMD nodes clean and avoid the high-latency software path.

infra-bot: alert: rocm_kernel_unavailable spike detected: +42% over 15m window. See /observability/alerts/ROCM_KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE

sagar: Good short-term. Longer term we should have the autotuner emit a per-arch availability blob that the router consumes. Two ideas:
- publish kernel_availability.json (arch -> seq_ranges -> kernels)
- runtime should expose a fast capability probe API (gRPC) so router can be consistent at request time without a DB hop

alex.k: Agreed. Also propose we add a metric counter 'runtime.kernel.fallback.reason' with tags {arch, seq_bucket, model}. That will make alerts and dashboards actionable.

mei: For the autotuner side, plan:
1) extend generation to include boundary seqs (512, 768, 1024) for gfx1030 on warmup runs
2) when compile budget exhausted, publish placeholder entries with 'compile_in_progress' to avoid silent false positives

tasha: I can open a hotfix PR to add the routing rule + a canary flag in console. We'll route seq>=768 away from AMD for the next 24-48h while we push the kernels.

alex.k: Can we also add an eval traffic canary to watch quality regressions for models routed to CPU/NVIDIA? want to ensure no downstream quality surprises.

mei: I'll add the kernel availability endpoint and bump autotuner job to run the missing targets. ETA for compiled kernels: ~36h if CI / compile cluster is healthy.

sagar: Action items:
- tasha: hotfix routing rule + alert suppression for 24h (PR link when ready) :shipit:
- mei: publish availability API + schedule autotuner runs (track compile job) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- alex.k: create dashboard panels for fallback counters and seq-bucket latency

alex.k: thanks all. Keep thread updated with PRs/CI links. If we see another spike, we'll toggle the canary and drain AMD pool.

infra-bot: deploy:hotfix-rocm-seq-guard started by tasha — build #5021 queued

mei: noted — I'll watch compile cluster logs and post progress here.

sagar: good catch. :thumbsup:
